result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.
Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.
Use transaction, ad-hoc or compensation behavior only when its specific semantics are explicitly described.

When the description assigns different actions to distinct ranges or levels of a measured value: Model a decision gateway with conditional outgoing flows that lead to the action for each range or level.

When the description identifies multiple distinct items that must be prepared or verified before a later step.: Model each actionable preparation or verification as a separate activity before the dependent activity, preserving stated dependencies.

result.rule: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.

result.rule: When the description distinguishes activities or outcomes by their action, object, recipient, or stage: Use BPMN labels that preserve those stated distinctions rather than substituting a different action or outcome.

When the description names alternative actions that can each signal or cause the same subsequent step: model each stated alternative as a distinct activity or event and preserve its path to the shared step, rather than omitting an alternative or substituting a different action

When the description explicitly states an activity’s action, object, recipient, or multiple coordinated actions: Preserve those stated details in the BPMN task label rather than omitting or substituting them.

When the description states an activity or outcome whose surrounding context is already clear from the process flow: Use a concise BPMN label that preserves the activity or outcome, without adding explanatory context that does not distinguish it from other elements.
